steps.title: Three steps to bring AI creation into your classroom
steps.lead: From setting up your school to students submitting real work — no tech team needed, and no accounts or API keys for students to bring.

items.title: Set up your school and accounts
items.desc: Allocate seats and authorizations, then create teacher and student accounts. Students sign in with the school account — no API key required.

items.title: Schedule straight from the course packs
items.desc: Ready-made course packs and teaching slides: pick a lesson and teach. Classes need zero setup — any lab computer will do.

items.title: Real work in every class, kept in your gallery
items.desc: Students make something worth showing with AI in every lesson. Submitted work goes to the gallery and becomes your school's case library and marketing material.

videos.title: Real work made in real classrooms
videos.lead: One piece per lesson — click to see what students actually built.

compare.title: The same AI class, two very different ways.
compare.lead: Tools, environment, accounts and work are all handled by the platform. Teachers just teach.

cards.title: Pieced together
items: Switching between many sites and apps breaks the rhythm of the lesson
Students register their own accounts and bring API keys — hard to manage, easy to leak
Teachers prepare slides and assets by hand, starting over every lesson
Work scatters across chat groups and personal laptops — nothing is kept
Problems get debugged live, turning teachers into IT support
Nothing can be reused across campuses; every new teacher starts from zero

cards.title: With Lingdong AI
items: One workbench for conversation, preview and project files
The school issues accounts and authorizations — students bring no keys
Standard course packs and slides are ready to teach, with zero setup
Work is submitted in class and goes straight to the gallery
Usage and compute are logged and visible, so costs stay clear
One process any campus or new teacher can repeat
